results.name: WP-17 lexer oracle: 28 edge cases module lexers are known to get wrong (strings / comments / templates / regexes containing import, member and method named import, regex after while / export default / of / return / typeof / a newline, division vs regex, hashbang, import attributes, \u escapes, export * as, string-named imports, dynamic import with options and plain templates) — the specifier ranges are IDENTICAL to acorn's

WP-17 lexer, function / class EXPRESSION vs DECLARATION (TT42; TT41 refused these files — and one shape was silently MISSED, not refused): after an expression body's "}" a slash divides, after a declaration's it starts a regex — 15 shapes identical to acorn (V8 when acorn itself mis-lexes), including named / async / generator function expressions, class expressions with heritage, a declaration followed by a regex statement, and export default function

WP-17 import.meta: every READ of import.meta.url becomes the module's real URL and import.meta.resolve is wrapped; an assignment target, import.meta.urlx and a string are left alone; the wrapper decodes a proxied URL back and passes any other through

WP-17 specifiers and import maps: root-relative, relative, absolute and protocol-relative http(s) specifiers are proxied with the module-graph segment; bare, data:, blob: and already-proxied ones are not; an import map's URL-like KEYS and every address are proxied the same way (so a rewritten specifier still prefix-matches a rewritten key), bare keys stay, scopes are mapped, "integrity" is dropped, malformed JSON is untouched

WP-17 / WP-19 HTML wiring: an inline module's specifiers and import.meta.url are rewritten (a classic inline script's dynamic import too, without import.meta), an inline import map is rewritten, a body the HTML parser split at a "</script>" inside a string is left unchanged, crossorigin elements / module scripts / modulepreload carry the CORS segment (":i" for use-credentials), and an iframe names its parent document (":f") while links and forms stay plain navigations

WP-17 root import map: a document with an id gets an import map routing run-time ROOT-RELATIVE module URLs ("/" → the site's root through the proxy, "/api/wp/s/" → itself so proxied URLs are untouched), injected right after the runtime when the page has none, MERGED into the page's own first map when it has one (one map per document, the page's own "/" key wins), using the final <base> origin; documents without an id get none

WP-18 segments: every legal flag combination round-trips through parseSidSegment / flagString / decodeTarget in canonical order; out-of-order, repeated or unknown flags, a flag on "r" / "f", and a short document id are all rejected

WP-18 redirect chains (Fetch §4.4 / §4.1): A→B→C taints the origin (Origin "null") and marks the chain cross-origin and cross-site; A→B→A taints too and keeps the request non-same-origin (no same-origin cookies, origin-only Referer, Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site); A→A stays clean; flags are sticky (never cleared by a later hop); mode same-origin refuses the cross-origin hop

WP-19 frame tree: a document registered with cross-site ancestors (xs) keeps that through the LRU; its subresources and script requests are cross-site for SameSite even to its OWN origin, while Sec-Fetch-Site and Origin still follow the document's origin; documentCsp drops frame-ancestors only for a validated nested frame
